reuse.why: Builds on the existing WeekendRule/applyWeekendRule/getDateWithSkippedWeekend chain and RSchedule/recurConfigToRSchedule, extending them for holidays and adding one shared getRecurOccurrences used by getNextDate, getUpcomingDates and the new range handler.

duplication.why: The config-to-WeekendRule mapping (including the frequency==='daily' derivation) is written twice (getWeekendRule in app.ts and inline in getNextDate) and a third, incomplete time in schedule-template.ts without the daily flag; getNextDate also queries occurrences twice.

placement.why: Weekend/holiday/daily logic lives in shared/schedules.ts next to the existing weekend helpers and the handler in server/schedules/app.ts alongside get-upcoming-dates; only the WeekendRule builder sits privately in app.ts instead of shared.

scope.why: Changes stay on schedules, weekend rule, types and the template/rule-utils field plumbing needed for the four steps; tests added accordingly.

maintainability.why: getRecurOccurrences is a reasonable single entry point, but the daily rule leaks into getNextDate as `skipWeekend && (isDaily || !noSkipWeekend)`, the candidate/window sizing heuristics scale with holiday count, and three call sites hand-build the rule differently.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All paths route date adjustment through applyWeekendRule/getRecurOccurrences; schedule-template still uses applyWeekendRuleToDay as before (its rule lacks the daily flag but daily skipping happens inside getNextDate).

disguised_duplication.where: The WeekendRule mapping repeated in app.ts getWeekendRule and shared getNextDate is plain repetition over differently named source fields, not a disguised copy.

abstraction_drift.where: WeekendRule gains `daily` and `holidays`, getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains `holidays`; special cases: daily drop branch in getRecurOccurrences (with holiday-scaled take) and the `isDaily || !noSkipWeekend` override in getNextDate; schedule-template.ts builds its own weekend rule without `daily`, relying on getNextDate instead of the shared mapping.
